title: Knowledge Check 9 - Lessons 41-45
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 41-45 - Data Enhancements, Sharing, and Analysis | Data Activations and Utilization. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A team has trained a predictive model in AI Models, but no segment can filter on the prediction. What is the missing step?
options: Retrain the model with more features
Run a prediction job or a batch data transform to write the predictions to a Data 360 object, then segment on that field
Move the model out from under the Einstein Trust Layer
Convert the model into a calculated insight
questions.explanation: Training produces the model, but the predictions must be generated and written to a Data 360 object before any segment can filter on them. Retraining changes the model rather than where its output lives, the trust layer is not something to remove, and a calculated insight is a different Data 360 object.

questions.question: Which statement about evaluating a trained classification model is TRUE?
options: Training metrics are only available for generative models
A lower AUC score is always better
The AUC score measures how well the model separates the positive and negative classes, and the ROC curve plots the true positive rate against the false positive rate
Training metrics cannot be viewed after training
questions.explanation: The AUC score rates class separation and the ROC curve plots true positive rate against false positive rate across thresholds. Higher AUC is better, the metrics are viewable after training, and they apply to predictive classification models.

questions.question: A customer wants to use a model built in Databricks alongside models built natively in Data 360. What does AI Models provide?
options: A requirement to copy the Databricks model into a CRM custom object first
A prompt template that rebuilds the model inside Data 360
Nothing, because only native models can be consumed in Salesforce
A bring your own model path that connects predictive models from external platforms such as Databricks so their predictions can be consumed across Salesforce
questions.explanation: AI Models supports bringing your own model by connecting predictive models built in external platforms such as Amazon SageMaker, Google Cloud Vertex AI, or Databricks, and their predictions can then be consumed across Salesforce. Native only, copying into a CRM object, and prompt templates describe paths the platform does not use.

questions.question: A team wants an agent to answer questions from internal documents and from customer data in Data 360. What must be configured for the documents to be retrieved?
options: Nothing, because the language model already knows the documents
Connect the content and create a search index that chunks and vectorizes it
Add the documents as CRM record fields only
Disable the Einstein Trust Layer for retrieval
questions.explanation: Retrieval augmented generation pulls context from a search index, so the content must be connected and indexed into chunked, vectorized data before an agent can retrieve it. The model does not already know your documents, record fields alone do not index them, and the trust layer is not disabled for retrieval.

questions.question: Which statement about the Einstein Trust Layer is TRUE?
options: Grounding data is retrieved regardless of the user's permissions
Prompts are grounded only with data the executing user can access, and prompts, responses, and trust signals are logged as an audit trail in Data 360
Customer data is used to train the language model
Toxicity scoring replaces the need for permissions
questions.explanation: Secure data retrieval grounds the prompt only with data the executing user can access, preserving role based controls and field level security, and the layer logs prompts, responses, and trust signals as an audit trail stored in Data 360. Customer data is not used to train the model, and toxicity scoring does not replace access controls.

questions.question: A prompt must include a value computed by an Apex process and an attribute from a Data 360 data model object. Which approach fits?
options: Grounding with merge fields, which can source record fields, flow or Apex values, and Data 360 data model objects
Hard coding the values into the prompt text
Using CRM record fields only, because Data 360 objects cannot be used
Vectorizing the values before every prompt
questions.explanation: Prompt Builder grounds with merge fields, and those fields can source CRM record fields, values produced by a flow or Apex, Data 360 data model objects, and related lists. Hard coding is not grounding, Data 360 objects are supported, and vectorizing is part of building the search index, not something done per prompt run.

questions.question: A consultant must explain what a Data 360 segment actually evaluates when it runs. Which statement is correct?
options: A segment filters raw source rows from the original systems
A segment filters a data model object such as Unified Individual, so it counts one member per unified profile
A segment joins data lake objects directly with no model mapping
A segment only reads calculated insights, never attributes
questions.explanation: Segments run on mapped data model objects and count one member per unified profile, not one per source row, and they read attributes as well as insights.

questions.question: A team wants an audience they can schedule and publish to a marketing destination. Which choice fits?
options: A dynamic segment
A real-time segment
A standard segment
A calculated insight
questions.explanation: Only a standard segment persists membership and can be scheduled and published; dynamic segments are API only, real-time segments cannot be manually published, and a calculated insight is a metric not an audience.

questions.question: Segment membership counts keep coming in lower than the business expects. Which factor best explains the gap?
options: The activation target is paused
The lookback window limits the data range, and container criteria can narrow it further
Segment membership objects are only written monthly
The segment was built on a custom data model object
questions.explanation: The lookback window bounds the data considered and a container window narrower than the segment level window takes precedence, shrinking the range; a paused target does not change segment membership.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the recommended way to design a new segment?
options: Open the data model object with the most fields and filter until the count looks reasonable
State the business goal as audience, condition, and action, then map each part to an object, criteria, and a destination
Build the largest possible audience and let the campaign team narrow it
Base the segment only on data lake objects
questions.explanation: Design begins with the goal expressed as audience, condition, and action, then maps to an object, criteria, and a destination; data-first design and unordered audiences produce unused or wrong segments.

questions.question: A consultant must build an audience of people whose criteria rely on recent order behavior. What is the best approach?
options: Segment on the Segment Membership object
Segment on Sales Order so each order becomes a member
Segment on Unified Individual and reach order attributes through relationships
Segment on a data lake object holding the raw orders
questions.explanation: To reach people, build on Unified Individual and traverse to order data through relationships; segmenting on Sales Order yields orders, and data lake objects are not segmentable targets.

questions.question: A segment preview returns fewer members than expected. Which cause is most likely?
options: The segment type was standard instead of dynamic
The data space is not the default space
The activation target is disconnected
The lookback window or a container whose criteria override it narrowed the data range
questions.explanation: A narrow lookback window or a container that overrides it shrinks the data range and drops members; preview is available to users with the right segment and data permissions.

questions.question: A consultant needs a segment whose criteria reference a customer lifetime value score computed across several sources. What should be used?
options: A data lake object attribute copied into the segment
A calculated insight added as a segment criterion
A data space filter
A primary key qualifier
questions.explanation: Calculated insights are metrics computed across data and can be added to extend a segment, which is exactly how criteria reference a computed value rather than a raw attribute.

questions.question: Which statement about the lookback window is correct?
options: It applies only to dynamic segments
It has no effect once the segment is saved
Container criteria can specify a narrower window that takes precedence over the segment level setting
It defaults to 30 days and cannot be changed
questions.explanation: Container criteria take precedence over the segment level window; the default is 90 days and can extend to your organization maximum, and it applies to standard segments generally.

questions.question: A segment built on a data model object with a composite key returns inaccurate counts. What does the documentation recommend?
options: Switch to a real-time segment
Remove the lookback window
Add more match criteria
Use data model objects with a single, unique primary key for segmentation
questions.explanation: The segment canvas relies on single field relationships and cannot join on all fields of a composite key, so the recommendation is to use a data model object with a single unique primary key.
